paragraphs.source_en: The large wild African fauna represented in the Round Head paintings testify that this artistic style developed during a humid phase. So which climatic phase amongst the various oscillations and which period of the Central Saharan prehistory best suit the Round Head complex? Based on the climatic record in the Acacus (Cremaschi & Di Lernia 1996a; 1998) a possible human occupation can be reconstructed. The period of abundant precipitation which started at around 15,600 BP, was preceded by an arid phase starting at roughly 20,000 BP. The period between 20,000 and 10,000 BP has been interpreted as totally arid with no life existing in the Sahara (e. g. Hugot 1974; Muzzolini 1995a).

paragraphs.source_en: Little research has been undertaken in the Central Sahara in terms of the palaeoclimate and, above all, the research that has been conducted has not been at a high spatial and temporal resolution (Vernet 2002). Aumassip (2004) points out that low temporal resolution in previous studies led to blocks of several millennia appearing either completely arid or completely humid. This is certainly not the case, as recent studies have confirmed numerous minor arid-humid oscillations within each phase (Vernet 2002; Maley 2004; Gasse 2006). Furthermore, different regions responded differently to the climatic changes. Therefore, the arid period which started at 20,000 BP did not cause the whole of the Central Sahara to become desert but rather there were several minor moist phases in a generally dry period which occurred in various areas.
